nodes.name: safety.py
nodes.summary: Holds the Computer Use engine's safety-confirmation handshake state so AgentLoop can await prompts while the REST confirm endpoint resolves them without a circular import.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level dicts keyed by session_id store asyncio.Event, decision, and a per-prompt nonce checked with hmac.compare_digest.

nodes.name: get_or_create_event
nodes.summary: Returns the session's existing asyncio.Event or creates and registers a new one.

nodes.name: arm
nodes.summary: Arms a fresh cleared Event, drops any prior decision, and mints a urlsafe nonce so the confirm endpoint cannot race a stale waiter.

nodes.name: verify_nonce
nodes.summary: Constant-time check that the supplied nonce matches the session's armed prompt nonce.

nodes.name: set_decision
nodes.summary: Signals an already-armed Event without creating a new one, so a late confirm cannot resurrect a waiter the loop no longer awaits.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Drops the session's pending Event, decision, and nonce after the prompt is resolved or cancelled.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for Computer Use Platform v2 backend primitives and HTTP API. Contains only the package docstring.

nodes.name: dev.py
nodes.summary: Local developer launcher that optionally bootstraps the repo, clears backend/frontend ports, restarts docker compose, then supervises the FastAPI backend and Vite frontend.
nodes.languageNotes: Windows vs POSIX branches for port discovery (netstat/lsof/ss), process kill (taskkill vs SIGTERM), and Vite spawn (node vite.js vs npm run dev).

nodes.name: open_dashboard_when_ready
nodes.summary: Polls a ready URL and opens the dashboard in the default browser once HTTP succeeds, or logs a manual-open hint on timeout.

nodes.name: _wait_for_http
nodes.summary: Blocks until a loopback URL responds or the watched process exits, then raises if the backend never becomes ready.

nodes.name: _dotenv_values
nodes.summary: Parses the repo-root .env into a key/value map, skipping comments and unquoted blanks.

nodes.name: _env_int
nodes.summary: Reads a port-like integer from the process env or dotenv, rejecting non-integers and values outside 1–65535.

nodes.name: _listening_pids_for_port
nodes.summary: Finds PIDs listening on a TCP port via netstat on Windows or lsof/ss on POSIX.

nodes.name: _process_command_line
nodes.summary: Returns a process command line via Win32_Process on Windows or ps on POSIX, used when logging port cleanup.

nodes.name: _terminate_pid
nodes.summary: Force-kills a PID with taskkill /T /F on Windows, or SIGTERM then SIGKILL on POSIX, skipping the launcher itself.

nodes.name: _clear_port
nodes.summary: Stops every listener on a port and waits until the port is free, raising if cleanup times out.

nodes.name: _terminate_process
nodes.summary: Stops a supervised Popen child with CTRL_BREAK on Windows or terminate elsewhere, then kills if it ignores the wait.

nodes.name: _spawn_services
nodes.summary: Starts backend.main, waits for /api/health, then starts Vite (node vite.js on Windows, npm run dev elsewhere).

nodes.name: _watch_processes
nodes.summary: Supervises backend and frontend until one exits or Ctrl+C, then tears down both processes and docker compose.

nodes.name: _parse_args
nodes.summary: Defines CLI flags for bootstrap, port-clearing, and opening the dashboard when Vite is ready.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates optional setup, port cleanup, compose restart, service spawn, optional dashboard opener, and process watch.

nodes.name: agent_service.py
nodes.summary: In-container ThreadingHTTPServer that exposes /health, /screenshot, and /action for X11 desktop automation via xdotool, scrot, and wmctrl, with token auth and a minimal engine action allowlist.
nodes.languageNotes: Strips xdotool --sync (hangs on compositor-less Xvfb) and substitutes configurable sleeps. Request-scoped action_id lives on threading.local because each request is its own thread.

nodes.name: _blocked_cmd_match

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what Computer Use Workbench v3.0.3 is: a local, single-user workbench for provider-native Computer Use agents on three routes (GPT-5.6 Luna / OpenAI Responses, Claude Sonnet 5 / Anthropic Messages, and Gemini 3.6 Flash / Google Interactions). TECHNICAL.md then names the pieces the rest of the tour unpacks — a single-process FastAPI runtime, typed /api/v2, CUAF binary frames, SQLite audit retention, and a React dashboard served from the same process. Read these first so later files land in a known architecture rather than as isolated modules.

tour.title: Runtime Startup
tour.description: The documented START.bat path bootstraps Windows prerequisites and hands off to the local launcher. dev.py optionally sets up the repo, clears backend and frontend ports, restarts Docker Compose, then supervises FastAPI and Vite together. backend/main.py is the process entry: it configures logging, enforces the public-bind guardrail, and starts Uvicorn, which serves the FastAPI app in backend/server/__init__.py. infra/config.py loads the environment-backed Docker, screenshot, bind, and API-key settings that every later backend module reads.
tour.languageLesson: Python process entry points typically guard startup with `if __name__ == "__main__"` so importing the module in tests does not bind a port. Uvicorn then loads the FastAPI `app` as an ASGI application.

tour.title: V2 API Contract
tour.description: Building on the FastAPI app from Step 2, backend/v2/api.py is the typed /api/v2 router for models, credential sessions, Google OAuth, agent sessions, analytics, retention, and workflows. v2/models.py loads the transport-aware catalog from computer_use_models.v2.json and rejects any entry that cannot do computer use. routing.py then applies deterministic multi-route fallback with per-route retries, retry-after backoff, and a failure-threshold circuit breaker so one provider outage does not strand an operator session.
tour.languageLesson: A FastAPI APIRouter mounts a versioned contract (`/api/v2`) onto the main app so the public HTTP surface stays independent of engine internals. Pydantic models on the router are the live schema the dashboard later consumes as camelCase JSON.

tour.title: Execution Coordination
tour.description: When a v2 session starts through the contract in Step 3, orchestrator.py bridges it to the existing Computer Use engine with task tracking, event fan-out, and cancel support. loop.py maps provider turns to step records, scrubs secrets, and handles stop, stuck-agent, and safety confirmation. engine/__init__.py selects the Gemini, Claude, or OpenAI client and wraps the desktop executor with safety policy; executor.py turns tool calls into sandbox HTTP actions; adapters.py normalize each vendor payload into a provider-neutral CanonicalAction.
tour.languageLesson: Python generators (and async generators) yield turn events as they happen, so the orchestrator can fan out live updates without waiting for the full run to finish.

tour.title: Durable Audit State
tour.description: Every coordinated run from Step 4 is written down. persistence.py is the SQLite WAL store for v2 sessions, actions, events, metrics, workflow versions, and safety checkpoints. retention.py writes hashed audit frames to disk and evicts them by age and byte budget, while observability.py records redacted, session-correlated traces with replay and invariant checks. storage.py is the process-wide upload store that keeps reference files inside extension, size, magic-byte, and session caps so audit history stays complete without leaking binaries into the database.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) lets readers continue while a writer appends. That fits a single-operator workbench that records audit events and serves the dashboard from one process.

tour.title: Dashboard Entry
tour.description: The operator surface is a five-tab React dashboard served by the same FastAPI process started in Step 2. main.tsx bootstraps the application and global styles. App.tsx is the workbench shell: sidebar navigation, token and shutdown controls, a route error boundary, and pages for live sessions, audit, workflows, provider credentials, and analytics. types.ts defines the shared TypeScript shapes those pages use when they consume the camelCase /api/v2 contract from Step 3 and the durable session records from Step 5.
tour.languageLesson: A React error boundary catches render errors in its children so one failed tab does not take down the whole workbench shell. createRoot in main.tsx is the single mount point that attaches that shell to the page.

tour.title: Browser Communication
tour.description: The dashboard from Step 6 talks to the backend on two channels. api.ts is the typed JSON client for /api/v2, including session-storage token helpers, ApiError, and shutdown. useLiveStream.ts opens an authenticated WebSocket, buffers stream events, and turns binary CUAF frames into object-URL images. protocol.ts decodes those frames in the browser; frames.py on the backend defines the same codec and coalesces concurrent screenshot captures onto one in-flight task so live preview stays in lockstep with the execution loop from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Binary WebSocket frames carry screenshot pixels more cheaply than base64 JSON. The encoder and decoder must share a fixed CUAF layout so the React hook can create object URLs without parsing a text envelope.

tour.title: Operator Workflow
tour.description: USAGE.md is the operator handbook for the five-tab dashboard: installation, provider login, safety confirmations, v1/v2 REST scripting, environment variables, and troubleshooting. credentials.py is the process-local vault behind the credentials tab — it holds API keys and Google OAuth tokens in memory with TTL expiry and never serializes secrets. deployment.md then shows how a single operator runs the START.bat path from Step 2, backs up the SQLite store from Step 5, and hardens public bind for a production-style local run.

tour.title: Sandbox Container
tour.description: Computer Use actions from Step 4 land in an isolated desktop, not on the host. docker-compose.yml defines the sandbox service, ports, and required secrets; Dockerfile builds the Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE/Xvfb image with Chrome, Firefox ESR, VS Code, a non-root agent user, and the in-container runtime. agent_service.py is that runtime: a ThreadingHTTPServer exposing /health, /screenshot, and /action with token auth and a tight action allowlist. backend/infra/docker.py starts the container, injects the token env-file, and caches readiness so the executor can call the agent HTTP API.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose `ports` and environment files keep VNC, noVNC, and the agent-service port on the local machine. The image's ENTRYPOINT/CMD is what starts Xvfb, the desktop, and agent_service.py together when the container runs.

tour.title: Quality Gates
tour.description: Quality gates lock the contracts you just walked. docs/codebase/TESTING.md maps pytest, Vitest, static checks, CI coverage, and mock strategy. test_v2_platform.py covers the catalog, SQLite store, routing, credential vault, CUAF frames, and HTTP contracts from Steps 3–5 and 7; test_provider_run_contract.py locks provider streaming, planner-before-computer-use order, and Gemini/Anthropic edge cases. ci.yml is the GitHub Actions workflow that runs backend, frontend, container build, dependency audits, and an image security scan on every change.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers, parallel `jobs`, and sequential `steps`. Splitting backend, frontend, and image jobs — and caching dependency installs — keeps the gate fast without dropping container or audit checks.
